newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal communists win two seats in by-elections.
newsitem.headline: Nepal communists win two seats in by-elections.

text.p: Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba's Nepali Congress party suffered early losses in parliamentary by-elections with two seats falling to the opposition communists, government officials said on Saturday.
The communists have won the prestigious Kathmandu One constituency and also the Sunsari Five seat in eastern Nepal, the Himalayan kingdom's Election Commission said.
Nepalis voted on Friday in the by-elections which were the first popular vote since Deuba's centrist Nepali Congress party formed a fractious coalition government in September 1995.
The Commission said the opposition Communist Unified Marxist-Leninist (UML) retained the Kathmandu seat, and ejected the Nepali Congress from the Sunsari constituency.
A commission spokesman told Reuters that votes were still being counted in the third constituency while results for two other by-elections were expected by late Monday or Tuesday.
Analysts see the outcome of Friday's ballots as key to Deuba's political future ahead of his next show of strength with the communists.

The UML, which has 87 deputies in the 205-member parliament, is the largest party in the national assembly but the Nepali Congress, which has 86 votes, commands a majority with the help of its partners: the Rashtriya Prajatandra Party, which has 19 members, and the Nepal Sadbhavana Party which has two deputies.
But the RPP is sharply divided over whether to continue with Deuba or join the communists.
Deuba survived a no-confidence vote last month but has promised to call a confidence vote when parliament convenes next month.
Parliamentary elections are not scheduled until 1999 in the kingdom, which ushered in multi-party rule in 1990 under a constitutional monarchy after a bloody pro-democracy movement.
